schema.title: STRATA_v2_DomainTreeSchema
schema.description: Canonical 5-axis Pydantic v2 domain manifest schema for STRATA (Symbolic Topological Routing Architecture for Typed Automata).

tree_structure.domain: string (unique domain identifier matching filename stem, e.g. cv2, pandas, audio, sqlite3)
tree_structure.description: string (concise technical summary of the domain plugin)
tree_structure.is_core: boolean (true only for foundational language/type/control-flow trees; false for swappable domain plugins)
tree_structure.aliases: array of strings (natural-language / package-name aliases recognized when scoping domains, e.g. ['opencv', 'cv'])
tree_structure.imports: array of strings (domain-level default import statements)
tree_structure.types: object mapping domain carrier names -> {'parent': '...', 'description': '...'} in the bounded poset
tree_structure.top_types: array of top-level carrier type names declared in this tree
tree_structure.language_spec: optional LanguageSpec object (declared in core language trees for backend-agnostic lowering)

cell_fields.cell_id: string (UNIQUE screaming snake-case or namespaced identifier, e.g. CV2_CANNY, PD_TO_CSV)
cell_fields.docstring: string (concise technical docstring for semantic retrieval & developer clarity)
cell_fields.code_template: string (syntax-valid Python template using {port_name} placeholders, e.g. {out} = cv2.Canny({image}, {threshold1}, {threshold2}))
cell_fields.code_templates: optional object mapping language name -> template when multi-backend
cell_fields.dependencies: array of strings (exact import statements required by code_template)
cell_fields.inputs: object mapping input port_name -> canonical PortSchema
cell_fields.outputs: object mapping output port_name -> canonical PortSchema
cell_fields.primary_in: optional string naming the primary input data port
cell_fields.primary_out: optional string naming the primary output data port
cell_fields.effects: array of ConditionPredicate objects or strings declaring semantic postconditions / resource effects
cell_fields.bridge_profile: optional BridgeProfileSchema ({is_bridge, delta_axes, cost_tier, lossy, requires_intent, notes}) strictly for type-converting bridges
cell_fields.polymorphic_propagation: optional PolymorphicPropagationSchema ({preserves_layout, preserves_dtype, preserves_typestate, preserves_semantics, preserves_nominal, source_port})

port_fields.carrier: string (Axis 1 carrier / HKT: e.g. File[Image, PNG], List[Contour], Tuple[int, ...], ndarray, DataFrame, int, float, str, bool)
port_fields.typestate: string (Axis 3 canonical domain-qualified or domain typestate, e.g. cv2:color_bgr, any, written_to_disk)
port_fields.accepted_states: array of additional accepted typestate strings
port_fields.layout: optional LayoutContract ({rank, shape, dtype, rank_polymorphic, channel_count, channel_axis, length})
port_fields.required: boolean (true for mandatory positional/required args; false for optional config knobs with default_value)
port_fields.default_value: any (literal Python default value, or null)
port_fields.enum_values: optional array of allowed discrete constant values

PILImage.description: PIL.Image.Image instance (requires explicit bridge to/from ndarray)

canonical_examples.docstring: Loads an image from a file into a numpy.ndarray.

image_path.description: Filesystem path to the image file to decode.

flags.description: Flag that can take values of cv2.ImreadModes (e.g. cv2.IMREAD_COLOR=1, cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE=0).

output_var.description: Loaded image array with shape (H, W, 3) or (H, W).

canonical_examples.docstring: Extracts topological contours from a binary or edge image matrix using border-following.

image.description: 8-bit single-channel binary or edge image matrix.

mode.description: Contour retrieval mode: cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL=0, cv2.RETR_LIST=1, cv2.RETR_CCOMP=2, cv2.RETR_TREE=3.

contours.description: Detected contours returned as a list of numpy point coordinate arrays.

hierarchy.description: Optional topology hierarchy matrix of shape (1, N, 4).

canonical_examples.docstring: Write DataFrame to a comma-separated values (csv) file.
